short_name: no premium within AEMO's published limit
basis: AEMO social licence inputs (S002) and landholder payment schemes (S003)
justification: The published per-MW expansion price already carries the community-engagement allowance inside the assumed lead time, the up-to-20% route lengthening around complex land, and the NSW and Queensland landholder payment schemes as cost categories, so charging a further premium inside the limit would double-count them.
used_for: Base tranche of the stepped premium
key: Premium on capacity from 0 to 1x the published limit

short_name: first tranche at AEMO's transmission cost impost
justification: 15% is the only published AEMO estimate of a transmission capital uplift for low social licence, and it is derived from costed scope changes that network businesses actually made in response to local stakeholder feedback; AEMO set it for projects inside the published limit, so applying it to the first step beyond the limit is a transfer of scope rather than of cost category.
used_for: Premium on the first relaxation tranche
key: Premium on capacity from 1x to 2x the published limit

short_name: second tranche at the top of AEMO's parcel-density ladder
basis: AEMO 2024 ISP social licence sensitivity (S001) with the land-contestation argument
justification: AEMO graduates its social licence uplift in proportion to private land parcel density, from a 5% floor at the reference density to 60% at twelve times it; capacity beyond the published limit is by construction on land the land-use screen excluded, so the top of AEMO's own range is preferred to inventing a number above it. The transfer from REZ generation build cost to transmission expansion cost, and the step from parcel density to a relaxation factor, are both unsourced.
used_for: Premium on the second relaxation tranche
key: Premium on capacity from 2x to 4x the published limit

short_name: premium applied to the price and not the ceiling
justification: Published per-MW expansion prices span two orders of magnitude, so a flat A$/MW adder would be a rounding error on the cheapest option and a doubling on the dearest; a percentage keeps the premium proportionate to what the option already costs.
key: Unit in which the premium is expressed
value: percentage of the option's published A$/MW

short_name: capacity-weighted easement length as the per-km conversion
justification: Every REZ and flow-path option publishes both its easement length and the capacity it adds, so a per-kilometre payment converts to a per-MW premium from AEMO's own data with no assumption about line voltage or rating.
used_for: Converting per-km landholder payments into a per-MW premium
value: 0.1494 km/MW for REZ options and 0.1121 km/MW for flow-path options

short_name: landholder payments treated as undiscounted totals
basis: NSW and Queensland scheme terms (S003 and S004)
justification: AEMO states the NSW rate as A$200000 per km paid in instalments over 20 years and the Queensland rate as a lump sum, so both are totals rather than annual rates and no annuity factor is applied; discounting the NSW instalments would lower its share of capex below the 2.8% reported.
used_for: Per-MW conversion of the payment schemes

short_name: violation penalties used to bound rather than to set the tranches
basis: REZ resource limit violation penalty factor (S006)
justification: AEMO's 0.3 A$M/MW in-REZ and 1.0 A$M/MW non-REZ penalties are the closest published analogue to pricing a megawatt built past a REZ limit, but they are chosen to make violation a last resort in the optimisation rather than estimated as a cost, so they bracket the proposal instead of setting it.
key: Implied premium bracket against the capacity-weighted REZ expansion cost

short_name: 4x treated as the outer relaxation rung
justification: AEMO's own scenario ladder raises REZ land-use limits by exactly 5.0x in the Accelerated Transition scenario, so a relaxation ladder stopping at 4x stays inside a range AEMO itself publishes, and no rung beyond 4x is proposed because nothing published supports one.
used_for: Outer bound of the stepped premium
